title: In-Memory MVCC B-Tree Storage Engine with WAL and ARIES Recovery
objective: Implement a high-performance, concurrent MVCC B+Tree storage engine in C++20 with Snapshot Isolation (SI), optimistic concurrent transactions, Write-Ahead Logging (WAL) with group commit, and deterministic ARIES crash recovery (Analysis, Redo, Undo). The engine must handle arbitrary concurrently interleaving read-write transactions, rollbacks, non-blocking garbage collection of obsolete tuple versions, and recover to a consistent state from simulated ungraceful process terminations (SIGKILL during active flushes).
motivation: Core transactional database engines require nuanced concurrency control, low-overhead latch management, and bulletproof crash recovery. Standard AI models struggle with complex concurrent B+Tree node splits under latch contention, dirty read visibility during cascading aborts, and WAL Log Sequence Number (LSN) ordering under crash-recovery scenarios.
difficultyExplanation:
1. Concurrent Node Splits & Structural Modifications: Implementing lock-free or latch-crabbing B+Tree structural modifications (page splits and merges) under high contention without deadlocks or dangling child pointers.
2. MVCC Visibility & Vacuuming: Managing monotonic commit timestamps, maintaining version chains with delta records, and executing safe background garbage collection without stalling active long-running readers.
3. ARIES Crash Recovery: Correctly implementing the 3-phase ARIES recovery algorithm (Analysis phase scanning from checkpoint to reconstruct Transaction Table and Dirty Page Table; Redo phase repeating history from min RecLSN; Undo phase scanning backwards to roll back uncommitted transactions and writing Compensation Log Records / CLRs).
environmentSummary: Ubuntu 22.04 base container with gcc-13, g++-13, cmake 3.28, ninja-build, valgrind, clang-tools-18, and Python 3.10 test harness pre-installed. The starter codebase in /app contains CMake build setup, public header interfaces (StorageEngine, Transaction, BufferManager, WAL, Page), and baseline unit test runners.
oracleStrategy: Reference C++20 implementation under solution/ provides a complete B-link tree with lock-free optimistic concurrency, an append-only ring buffer WAL with group commit synchronization, and a full ARIES state machine that guarantees exact recovery of committed state across abrupt process crashes.
verificationStrategy:
The verifier runs test.sh which executes four independent test channels:
1. Functional correctness (CRUD operations, range scans, abort/rollback).
2. Concurrent Transaction Stress Test (64 worker threads executing mixed read-write transactions with Jepsen-style history checking for Snapshot Isolation anomalies).
3. Crash Injection & Recovery (random SIGKILL during high write volume, followed by engine restart and state consistency verification against committed log records).
4. Sanitizer Pass (ASan and TSan checks ensuring zero memory corruption, use-after-free, or data races).
binarySuccessCondition: Passes all functional tests, Snapshot Isolation concurrency stress tests with zero data corruption, successfully recovers 100% of committed transactions following crash injection, and passes with 0 AddressSanitizer/ThreadSanitizer errors.
partialScoreStrategy:
Monotone scoring breakdown:
- 25%: Basic single-threaded CRUD, range scans, and manual transaction commit/abort.
- 25%: Multi-threaded concurrent transactions under Snapshot Isolation without deadlocks.
- 30%: Robust ARIES crash recovery and log replay under abrupt process termination.
- 20%: Zero race conditions, memory leaks, or synchronization anomalies under TSan/ASan.
anticipatedExploits:
1. Hard-coding synchronous fsync on every single write: verifier enforces throughput floor (>30,000 transactions/sec) and tests group commit batching.
2. In-memory bypass (ignoring WAL on disk): verifier injects process termination via SIGKILL, wipes RAM state, and boots the engine fresh from disk logs.
3. Using SQLite / LevelDB embedded library wrappers: verifier inspects symbols and static linking to ensure native B+Tree implementation is compiled from the codebase.
